quiz.title: Spot the Drift
quiz.q1.text: An AI gives exactly the right answer 10 times in a row. Can you conclude it will give the same answer tomorrow?
quiz.q1.rule: A favorable track record doesn't let you infer future behavior without continuous measurement.
quiz.q2.text: Same model, same question, two different answers. Is that automatically a problem?
quiz.q2.rule: A divergence (FLAG) isn't proof of an error, and a conflict between signals isn't a contradiction in itself.
quiz.q3.text: An AI stays perfectly consistent across 100 runs, but its answer is wrong. Is it "stable"?
quiz.q3.rule: Yes, it is stable — that's exactly the trap: stability measures consistency, not truth. An AI can be perfectly stable and wrong every single time. That's "deceptive stability": a high G score never guarantees factual accuracy, and responsibility for the decision stays human.
quiz.q4.text: Your AI system's behavior shifts subtly on a given day. What would you want to have?
quiz.q4.options: The ability to reproduce the event
quiz.q4.rule: Alert, trace, and reproducibility are the three conditions for provenance and temporal causality of the signal — no single one is enough on its own.
quiz.q5.text: If that trace is produced by a third party, what actually makes it usable?
quiz.q5.rule: Only a machine-readable, timestamped, verifiable artifact satisfies the ENF contract and freeze artifacts — a visual alone doesn't.
quiz.level.clear: None of the rules tested caught you out. That doesn't mean automatic trust — it means that, on these 5 cases, your reading was aligned with how NeoMundi interprets these signals.
quiz.level.watch: One or two reflexes deserve reinforcing before you rely on a stability signal without further verification.
quiz.level.unsettled: Several answers shouldn't be generalized routinely without additional review or independent judgment — see the RÉAGI breakdown below.
quiz.level.alert: On these test cases, explicit oversight would be required before letting a stability signal alone influence a high-consequence decision.
quiz.reveal.disclaimer: This result isn't a grade. It shows where your reading of AI behavior matches — or diverges from — how NeoMundi interprets these signals. The dashboard informs your judgment; it never replaces your responsibility.

v2.hero.subtitle: Observable AI behavior under constant reference conditions.
v2.hero.explainer: This status reflects how each system answers the same fixed reference question over time — not whether its answers today are right or wrong, and not proof that a provider changed a model internally.
v2.current_state.heading: Current longitudinal state — {n} systems
v2.current_state.empty: No longitudinal data available for this date yet.
v2.what_changed.empty: No significant behavioral change detected across the panel in this observation window.
v2.event.behavioral_deviation_detected: Behavior observed on the reference question diverged from its own baseline on this day — an isolated observation, not yet confirmed.
v2.event.persistent_deviation: Behavior on the reference question has differed from its established baseline for several consecutive days. This describes an observed, sustained change in behavior — it does not indicate or prove an internal change to the model.
v2.event.return_to_baseline: Behavior has returned to its usual reference range after a period of observed deviation.
v2.event.variability_increase: Answers to the reference question have become less consistent across repetitions than usual.
v2.event.coverage_anomaly: Insufficient data was collected on this day to evaluate behavior reliably. No behavioral conclusion is drawn.
v2.event.known_model_version_change: A change in the declared model identifier was observed on this date. Any behavioral change around this date may be related — this is a documented configuration fact, not an inference from behavior.
v2.event.model_identity_unverified: The exact model version queried for this system is not fully pinned or independently verifiable from the API response. Read any trend for this system with this in mind.

v2.methodology.heading: Methodology / Data
v2.methodology.stimulus_text: AI Weather's status comes from a single fixed reference question, repeated identically every day for every system — never the daily question shown in Today's Challenge.
v2.methodology.repetitions_text: Each system answers the reference question {n} times per day (V2.0 launch configuration). This value is versioned and may change in a future methodology version.
v2.methodology.baseline_text: Each system's baseline is its own median response over its first 14 valid measurement days — never compared across systems.
v2.methodology.dispersion_text: Deviations are measured in units of the baseline's own variability (MAD). A minimum floor, tied to the measurement's own resolution, prevents a very stable baseline from making ordinary variation look artificially extreme.
v2.methodology.uncertainty_text: A statistical uncertainty range is shown for transparency. It never decides the state shown — it only expresses how much confidence a small number of repetitions can support.
v2.methodology.separation_text: These are two independent measurements. Today's Challenge can never influence or determine the AI Weather status.
v2.methodology.identity_text: Where a system's exact model version cannot be independently confirmed from the API response, this is shown explicitly rather than assumed.
v2.methodology.versioning_text: Every measurement is stamped with the exact methodology and configuration version that produced it. A future change in method or repetition count creates a new version — past measurements are never recalculated retroactively.
v2.methodology.limits_text: An observed behavioral change is not proof that a provider modified a model. AI Weather reports observable behavior over time, not the internal state of a system.
